description.value: Mark Twain, an American author and orator, whose real name was Samuel Langhorne Clemens, was a pseudonym. "Mark Twain" was originally a term used by Mississippi River sailors to indicate the depth of water measured in the channel. His representative works include the novels *The Million Pound Note*, *Adventures of Huckleberry Finn*, and *Adventures of Tom Sawyer*. Mark Twain wrote extensively throughout his life, covering novels, plays, essays, and poetry. In terms of content, his works criticized injustices and the ugliness of human nature, expressing the strong sense of justice and concern for ordinary people of this writer who had worked as a typesetter and sailor.
